Overview

Embark on a breathtaking winter and spring journey through the heart of Skardu, an untouched paradise nestled in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. This 9-day adventure offers a mesmerizing blend of snow-covered landscapes, frozen lakes, and iconic valleys, making it perfect for those looking to experience the serenity and raw beauty of Northern Pakistan.

Why This Tour?

    • Scenic Winter & Spring Landscapes – Witness snow-clad valleys, frozen lakes, and dramatic desert dunes in winter, or vibrant spring blossoms and lush valleys as the region awakens from the cold.
    • Unforgettable Adventure – Visit Khaplu, Shigar, and Bashu Valley, explore ancient forts, and drive through dramatic mountain landscapes.
    • Unique Local Culture – Experience the traditional Balti culture, interact with warm and hospitable locals, and explore centuries-old palaces and villages.
    • Luxury & Comfort – Enjoy the perfect balance of adventure and relaxation, with carefully curated accommodations and expert-guided experiences.

Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad – Gateway to the North

Upon arrival at Islamabad International Airport, you will be welcomed by our team and transferred to your hotel. After checking in, take some time to relax before joining your fellow travelers for a warm welcome dinner. If time permits, enjoy a stroll through the bustling city streets or explore local markets before retiring for the night.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 2: Scenic Flight to Skardu – Gateway to the Karakoram

Start your day with a breathtaking flight from Islamabad to Skardu, soaring over some of the world’s tallest peaks, including Nanga Parbat. Upon arrival, take in the crisp mountain air as we explore Upper and Lower Kachura Lakes, both stunning in their icy winter or reflective spring beauty. Afterward, drive to the Shigar Valley, passing through the mystical Cold Desert and Blind Lake before reaching Shigar Fort, a historic fortress that has been transformed into a luxury stay.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Shigar Fort
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms Katpana
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 3: Chunda Valley & Katpana Desert – A Contrast of Landscapes

Today, journey to the stunning Chunda Valley, offering panoramic views of Skardu’s snow-covered landscapes. After soaking in the breathtaking scenery, head to the Katpana Cold Desert, one of the world’s highest deserts, where golden dunes are often dusted with snow in winter or surrounded by lush meadows in spring. Spend time exploring the unique terrain before heading back to the hotel for the evening.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Shigar Fort
  • Luxury: Destination Hotels
  • Standard: North Homes Khaplu

Day 4: Bashu Valley – Off-Road Adventure into the Wilderness

Prepare for an off-road adventure as we make our way to the pristine Bashu Valley, a secluded paradise surrounded by snow-capped peaks and dense forests. After navigating the rugged terrain, arrive in this untouched winter wonderland, where you’ll have the chance to take in the stunning views, explore the surroundings, and enjoy moments of peaceful solitude before returning to Skardu.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Byarsa Hotel
  • Luxury: Lokal Room Katpana
  • Standard: Eat and Read Hotel

Day 5: Discover the Beauty of Khaplu Valley

Begin the day with a drive to Khaplu Valley, a serene region known for its majestic landscapes, ancient architecture, and traditional Balti culture. Stop at Sailing Village, a charming riverside settlement, before exploring Khaplu Palace, an architectural masterpiece that dates back centuries. Spend the afternoon wandering through quaint villages and local bazaars, soaking in the peaceful ambiance of this hidden gem.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Serena Khaplu Palace
  • Luxury: Destination Hotel
  • Standard: North Homes

Day 6: Waterfalls & Wilderness – Manthoka & Khamoosh Falls

Today’s adventure takes us to Manthoka Waterfall, a spectacular cascading wonder surrounded by dramatic mountain landscapes. After spending some time enjoying the views, continue to Khamoosh Waterfall, another hidden treasure tucked deep within the valleys of Skardu. The drive itself is an experience, as we pass through some of the most scenic landscapes in Gilgit-Baltistan. Return to Skardu for a relaxing evening.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Byarsa Hotel
  • Luxury: Lokal Rooms
  • Standard: Katpana Eat and Read Hotel

Day 7: Return to Islamabad – A Day of Leisure

Fly back to Islamabad, where you will have the rest of the day to relax or explore the capital city. Enjoy a delicious dinner and unwind before your final day of sightseeing.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel

Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 8: Islamabad City Tour – A Cultural Exploration

Spend the day exploring Islamabad’s most iconic landmarks. Visit the Faisal Mosque, one of the largest and most beautiful mosques in South Asia, before heading to the Pakistan Monument and Museum, where you’ll gain insights into the nation’s history. Drive up to Daman-e-Koh, a viewpoint offering breathtaking panoramic views of Islamabad, and spend the evening at leisure.

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 9: Departure – Farewell Pakistan!

As your journey comes to an end, enjoy a final breakfast before transferring to Islamabad International Airport for your flight home. Depart with unforgettable memories of the stunning landscapes, vibrant culture, and thrilling adventures that Skardu has to offer.

Packing List

Spring Packing Checklist for Northern Pakistan - Summit Experts

Spring (late-March to May) is one of the best seasons to explore Northern Pakistan, with mild weather, blooming flowers, and lush green landscapes. To make sure you have a comfortable and enjoyable journey, we’ve prepared a comprehensive packing list for your adventure.

Essential Packing Categories:

  1. Luggage & Bags
    • Main Luggage (70-80L): A sturdy, spacious bag for all your essentials. Ensure it has waterproof covers for unexpected weather.
    • Daypack (30-40L): Ideal for carrying daily items like snacks, water, and your camera during excursions.
    • Padlocks: Secure your belongings during travel.
  2. Clothing
    • Upper Body:
      • Lightweight Jacket: Perfect for chilly mornings and evenings. Consider a windbreaker or fleece.
      • Long-Sleeve Shirts & T-Shirts: Comfortable, breathable fabrics are ideal for layering.
      • Rain Jacket: Waterproof and wind-resistant for unexpected spring showers.
    • Lower Body:
      • Trekking Trousers: Lightweight and quick-drying trousers for hikes and outdoor activities.
      • Comfortable Pants/Jeans: Suitable for both city tours and countryside visits.
    • General Tips:
      • Layer Up: The weather can vary, so layers will help you adjust to temperature changes.
      • Respect Local Culture: Modest clothing is recommended, especially in towns and cultural sites.
  3. Footwear
    • Hiking Boots: Well-worn, waterproof boots with good ankle support for trekking.
    • Comfortable Walking Shoes: For city exploration and casual outings.
    • Warm Socks: Preferably made of moisture-wicking material.
  4. Accessories
    • Sunblock (SPF 50+): Protects against strong UV rays.
    • Hat/Cap: For sun protection during hikes and outdoor tours.
    • Sunglasses: Good UV protection for your eyes.
    • Light Scarf/Bandana: Useful for dust protection and sun cover.
  5. Toiletries & Personal Care
    • Compact Toiletry Kit: Include essentials like toothpaste, deodorant, and moisturizer.
    • Travel Towel: Quick-drying and lightweight.
    • Wet Wipes & Hand Sanitizer: For maintaining hygiene during day trips.
  6. Hydration & Snacks
    • Reusable Water Bottle (Insulated Preferred): Stay hydrated, especially during hikes.
    • Energy Bars & Snacks: Lightweight snacks for quick energy boosts.
  7. Tech & Gadgets
    • Camera & Accessories: Capture stunning landscapes and cultural moments. Bring extra memory cards.
    • Power Bank: Essential for keeping devices charged on the go.
    • Travel Adapter: Ensure compatibility with local sockets.
  8. Important Documents
    • Passport: Must have at least six months of validity remaining.
    • Visa & Travel Insurance: Check visa requirements and carry printouts of your insurance details.
    • Emergency Contact Information: A printed list of important contacts.

Tips for Spring Travel

  • Prepare for Variable Weather: Spring can bring unexpected showers, so a waterproof jacket and protective covers for your belongings are recommended.
  • Comfortable Layers: Temperatures fluctuate, so plan for both warm afternoons and cool evenings.
  • Be Ready for Long Walks: Comfortable shoes and a light backpack will make your excursions more enjoyable.

Why Travel with Summit Experts?

Our experienced team ensures that your journey is not just comfortable, but also safe and unforgettable. We provide personalized packing recommendations based on your specific tour itinerary, and our guides are always ready to help you with any last-minute needs.

We trekked through some of the most breathtaking regions: Skardu, Hunza, Shimshal Village, and made our way to Shimshal Pass, ending with the exhilarating summit of Manglik Sar (6050m). From the very first moment, I knew I was in the hands of true professionals. The entire trip was perfectly organized, from the logistics to safety measures. But what truly made this experience stand out was the team. Every single person was warm, supportive, and treated me like family. Over the course of the trek, they all became a second family to me, and I genuinely feel like I’ve made lifelong friends. The beauty of the Karakoram combined with the knowledge, passion, and dedication of the Summit Experts team made this adventure unforgettable. I felt supported, safe, and inspired every single day. I don’t add pictures, because you MUST visit and see all the beauty of Pakistan with your own eyes. Nothing can compare to standing there in person, taking in the vastness and the majesty of the Karakoram range. Thanks to the expertise of Summit Experts, I felt safe and supported every step of the way. The team’s passion for the mountains and commitment to making sure each trekker has the best possible experience is what really sets them apart. This wasn’t just a trek—it was an unforgettable journey, and I already can’t wait to return. I’m already thinking about next year and planning to do even more trekking in Pakistan. There’s so much more to explore, and I wouldn’t want to do it with anyone else but Summit Experts. If you’re considering an adventure in Pakistan, I cannot recommend this company enough. Thank you, Summit Experts, for an experience I’ll never forget.

About Us

Welcome to Summit Experts

Adventure Tours

Our Legacy of
Adventure

At Summit Experts, we are more than a travel company — we are a community of passionate locals born and raised in the breathtaking Karakoram Mountains. From the high peaks of Gilgit-Baltistan to the living traditions of its valleys, our mission is to share the beauty, culture, and spirit of our homeland with explorers from around the world, while delivering journeys that are safe, authentic, and unforgettable.

Our story began with a shared dream: to create travel experiences that reflect both the grandeur of Pakistan’s mountains and the warmth of its people. That dream was carried by our founder, Shah Doulat — a mountaineer whose vision continues to guide everything we do today.

Whether you come to stand beneath an 8,000-metre giant or to wander the orchards, forts, and festivals of the north, you travel with a team whose roots run deep in these mountains. We don’t just show you the Karakoram — we share its stories, because they are our own.

Our Core Values
What drives us

Authenticity

Delivering genuine experiences rooted in local culture and natural beauty.

Safety First

Ensuring rigorous safety measures for all treks and tours

Sustainability

Championing eco-friendly tourism that supports local communities and protects the environment.

Excellence

Providing exceptional service through experienced guides and meticulous planning.

Remembering Shah Doulat — Founder of Summit Experts

Summit Experts was founded by Shah Doulat, a son of Shimshal — the legendary “Valley of Mountaineers” — whose life was shaped by the mountains he loved. From humble beginnings, Shah rose to become one of Pakistan’s most respected high-altitude mountaineers and a mentor to a generation of young guides.

Over his career, Shah summited some of the world’s most formidable peaks, including K2 (8,611m), Nanga Parbat (8,126m) — without supplemental oxygen — and Gasherbrum II (8,035m), alongside many other peaks and demanding trekking routes across the Karakoram. But Shah measured his life by more than summits. He believed in lifting up the next generation — training young guides, strengthening the safety and professionalism of Pakistani mountaineering, and proving to the world what local talent could achieve.

Shah is no longer with us, but his spirit lives on in every expedition we lead and every traveller we welcome. His legacy is not a memory we look back on — it is the foundation we build on, every single day.

Read Shah Doulat's Full Story

The Visionaries Behind Summit Experts

Summit Experts is driven by a dynamic team of adventurers, guides, and cultural experts. With Shah at the helm, our team blends youthful energy with decades of experience to deliver exceptional travel experiences. We are proud of the local talent that powers Summit Experts. 

Although some foreign‐run companies doubt local capabilities, we know our strength comes from within our communities. By partnering with digital experts from our own country, we leverage modern technology to deliver seamless and personalized travel planning. Our team’s deep roots in the Karakoram mean we don’t just show you these mountains—we share their stories and traditions in a way that no outsider can.

98+

Satisfaction Rate

500+

Satisfied Travelers

10+

Years of Experience

Why Summit Experts?

Summit Experts is your bridge to authentic adventure in Pakistan. We are proudly locally owned, and we believe the strength of a journey comes from the people who lead it. By keeping our expertise — and the economic benefits of tourism — within our own communities, we empower local families, preserve our traditions, and offer travellers something no outside operator can: a genuine connection to the land and the people who call it home.

Our guides blend years of mountaineering and cultural experience with modern planning and communication, ensuring your journey is both exhilarating and responsible. Whether you are scaling a peak or immersing yourself in a mountain festival, we are honoured to share our home with you.

Achieving the
Extraordinary

Summit Experts and Shah’s remarkable story have been featured in leading travel publications and media outlets, showcasing the transformative impact of their work on adventure tourism in Pakistan.

Trailblazers

Guided over 36 successful treks to K2 Base Camp, Fairy Meadows, and beyond.

Global Reach

Expanded operations to serve international travelers from over 6 countries, including France, Germany, the UK, and the US.

Building Excellence

Built one of Pakistan’s largest tourism logistics teams, operating across the Karakoram, Himalayas, & Hindukush regions.

Meet The Team
Behind Your Journey

Experienced guides and cultural experts dedicated to your adventure.

View All Team Members

Izhar Ali

Climbing Guide

Izhar Ali

Climbing Guide

Izhar Ali is a highly skilled climbing guide with extensive experience in the Karakoram Range. He has summited Gasherbrum II (2024), the Passu Cones (2021), and Minglik Sar, showcasing his exceptional technical expertise and endurance. Known for mastering challenging passes like Verjurav La and Khurdopin La, Izhar combines a deep commitment to safety with a passion for creating unforgettable mountaineering experiences.

Yousuf Ali

Climbing Guide

Yousuf Ali

Climbing Guide

An experienced climbing guide with an impressive record of high-altitude achievements. He successfully summited K2 , the world’s second-highest peak, and conquered the infamous Nanga Parbat, His ascent of Spantik Peak further highlights his technical expertise and resilience. With extensive knowledge of challenging terrains and a strong focus on safety, Yousuf ensures an exceptional mountaineering experience for every adventurer.

Tabasum Seher

Sightseeing Guide

Tabasum Seher

Sightseeing Guide

From the breathtaking Hunza Valley, Tabasum Seher is a skilled guide specializing in Gilgit-Baltistan and Chitral Valley tours. With deep cultural knowledge and warm hospitality, she leads travelers to iconic landmarks and hidden gems, ensuring seamless and unforgettable journeys.

Samana Rahim

Mountaineer & Guide

Samana Rahim

Mountaineer & Guide

From Shimshal Valley, Hunza, Samana Rahim is the second licensed female tourist guide in Pakistan and an accomplished mountaineer. She has guided climbs to peaks like Manglik Sar (6050m) and led an all-female team to its summit, championing women in mountaineering. With extensive trekking experience, Samana inspires adventure and promotes the beauty of northern Pakistan.

Overview

About Expedition

Broad Peak (8,051m) is the 12th highest mountain in the world, located in the Karakoram Range of Pakistan. This expedition offers climbers the chance to ascend one of the world’s most stunning 8,000-meter peaks, with expert logistics and local support to ensure a safe and successful climb.

Why Choose Us?

  • Experienced expedition logistics team.
  • Strong local connections for hassle-free operations.
  • High-quality meals and equipment at base camp.
  • Professional support for both independent and guided climbers.
  • Reliable weather forecasting and emergency assistance.
  • Commitment to environmental sustainability and responsible tourism.

Itinerary

Day 01: Arrive Islamabad, transfer to hotel.

Day 02: Fly to Skardu

Day 03: Briefing at Ministry of Tourism. Meeting with LO (Liaison Officer).

Day 04: Day free at Skardu.

Day 05: Free Day at Skardu for final preparation.

Day 06: Skardu – Askole (6-7 hrs)

Day 07: Trek to Jhula near Domardo River. (8-9 hours)

Day 08: Trek to Paiyu provides good views of Baltoro South, Cathedral Towers, and triangle of K2 at far view (5-7 hrs).

Day 09: Day free at Paiyu for acclimatization (3600 m).

Day 10: Trek to Urdukus: To Khuburtze (8-9 hrs): A gradual climb up Baltoro Glacier.

Day 11: Goro II: Trek across difficult side crevasses; camp at 4500 meters.

Day 12: Concordia: Spectacular views and gigantic mountain panorama, camp at 4700 m.

Day 13: 2-3 hours trek to Broad Peak base camp.

Day 14-37: Climb Broad Peak (depends on weather, fitness, experience).

Day 38-41: Return to Askole or Hushe and drive to Skardu.

Day 42: Fly to Islamabad or drive to Chilas.

Day 43: Day free at Islamabad or drive to Islamabad.

Day 44: De-briefing at the ministry of tourism.

Day 45: Fly to destination.

Packing List

Personal Gear

✔️ Backpack: 50-60 liter capacity, lightweight with compression straps and ice axe loops.
✔️ Daypack: 35-45 liter capacity for acclimatization hikes and approach treks.
✔️ Duffel Bags: Durable, waterproof bags for gear transport; recommended 90-120 liters.

Sleeping System

✔️ Sleeping Bag: Rated to at least -20°C (-4°F); down-filled preferred for its warmth-to-weight ratio.
✔️ Sleeping Pad: Inflatable or foam pad for insulation and comfort.
✔️ Sleeping Bag Liner: Adds warmth and keeps the sleeping bag clean.

Footwear

✔️ High-Altitude Mountaineering Boots: Insulated double or triple boots suitable for 8000-meter peaks.
✔️ Hiking Boots: Sturdy, well-broken-in boots for the trek to base camp.
✔️ Camp Shoes: Lightweight footwear for use around camp.
✔️ Gaiters: High-quality, waterproof gaiters to keep snow out of boots.
✔️ Socks: Multiple pairs of thermal mountaineering socks and liner socks.

Clothing

Base Layers
✔️ Thermal Underwear: Moisture-wicking, quick-drying tops and bottoms; merino wool or synthetic materials recommended.

Mid Layers
✔️ Insulated Jacket: Down or synthetic fill with a hood for added warmth.
✔️ Soft Shell Jacket and Pants: Breathable, water-resistant layers for protection against wind and light precipitation.

Outer Layers
✔️ Hard Shell Jacket and Pants: Durable, waterproof, and breathable; Gore-Tex or similar material.
✔️ Down Suit: Full-body suit designed for extreme cold at high altitudes.

Additional Clothing
✔️ Insulated Pants: Down or synthetic fill for high camps and summit attempts.
✔️ Fleece or Soft Shell Pants: For added insulation during colder conditions.
✔️ Gloves and Mittens: Layering system including liner gloves, insulated gloves, and expedition mittens.
✔️ Hats: Warm beanie and balaclava for head and face protection.
✔️ Neck Gaiter or Buff: Versatile protection for neck and face.

Climbing Equipment

✔️ Ice Axe: General mountaineering axe appropriate for your height.
✔️ Crampons: 12-point steel crampons compatible with your boots.
✔️ Climbing Harness: Lightweight, adjustable harness with gear loops.
✔️ Helmet: UIAA-certified climbing helmet.
✔️ Carabiners: Assorted locking and non-locking carabiners.
✔️ Belay/Rappel Device: ATC-style device compatible with rope diameter.
✔️ Ascender (Jumar): For fixed rope ascents.
✔️ Prusik Cord: 6mm cord for safety backups and crevasse rescue.
✔️ Trekking Poles: Adjustable, collapsible poles with snow baskets.

Accessories

✔️ Headlamp: High-output LED with extra batteries.
✔️ Sunglasses: Category 4 lenses for high-altitude sun protection.
✔️ Goggles: Anti-fog, UV-protective lenses for windy or snowy conditions.
✔️ Water Bottles: Two 1-liter wide-mouth bottles; insulated covers recommended.
✔️ Thermos: For hot drinks during cold conditions.
✔️ Personal First Aid Kit: Including blister care, personal medications, and high-altitude remedies.
✔️ Repair Kit: Duct tape, sewing kit, and repair materials for gear fixes.
✔️ Stuff Sacks/Dry Bags: For organization and waterproofing gear.
✔️ Camera: Optional, but ensure it’s durable and can withstand cold temperatures.
✔️ Notebook and Pen: For journaling or note-taking.

Personal Items

✔️ Passport and Permits: Ensure all necessary documents are up-to-date and accessible.
✔️ Insurance Documents: Proof of travel and evacuation insurance.
✔️ Cash: For incidental expenses and tips.
✔️ Toiletries: Biodegradable soap, toothbrush, toothpaste, floss, and other personal hygiene items.
✔️ Sunscreen: SPF 50+ for high-altitude exposure.
✔️ Lip Balm: With SPF protection.
✔️ Towel: Lightweight, quick-drying.
✔️ Earplugs: For restful sleep in communal settings.

Note: This list serves as a general guideline. Individual needs may vary based on personal
preferences and specific expedition requirements. Always consult with your expedition leader or
guide service to tailor the packing list to your needs.

FAQs

01

What skillset and fitness level are required for a Broad Peak expedition?

+

Climbing Broad Peak demands a high level of physical fitness and prior high-altitude mountaineering experience. Participants should be comfortable with long-duration climbs and possess technical skills in navigating mixed terrains of rock, snow, and ice. Training should include endurance exercises, strength training, and technical climbing practice.

02

What is the best season to climb Broad Peak?

+

The optimal climbing window for Broad Peak is during the summer months, typically from June to August. This period offers more stable weather conditions, which are crucial for a safer and more successful ascent.

03

How long does the Broad Peak expedition take?

+

A standard Broad Peak expedition spans approximately 45 days. This duration includes arrival in Islamabad, travel to Skardu, trekking to base camp, acclimatization periods, the summit attempt, and the return journey.

04

What is the typical daily schedule during the trek to base camp?

+

On trekking days, the routine generally involves waking up early, having breakfast at dawn, and trekking for 6–8 hours, depending on terrain and weather conditions. A lunch break is taken midday, with arrival at the next campsite by mid-afternoon, followed by rest, dinner, and briefings for the next day.

05

What type of accommodation is provided during the expedition?

+

During the trek to base camp and the climb, accommodation consists of full-service camping with tents provided. In cities like Islamabad and Skardu, accommodations are typically in hotels or guesthouses.

06

How is drinking water managed during the expedition?

+

Water is typically sourced from local streams and treated to ensure safety. It's advisable to bring personal water purification methods, such as Steripen or water treatment tablets, to further ensure water quality.

07

What are the communication facilities during the expedition?

+

Base camps are often equipped with communication facilities, including satellite phones and internet access via satellite modems. However, connectivity can be limited and is primarily used for essential communications.

08

What is the success rate for summiting Broad Peak?

+

Broad Peak is considered one of the safer 8,000-meter peaks, with a relatively higher success rate compared to others in its category. However, success depends on various factors, including weather conditions, climber experience, and acclimatization.

09

Are there any permit restrictions for climbers of certain nationalities?

+

Climbers of certain nationalities may face restrictions or additional scrutiny when obtaining permits for Broad Peak. It's essential to check with the relevant authorities or your expedition organizer to ensure compliance with current regulations.

10

What is the policy on tipping guides and porters?

+

Tipping is customary and greatly appreciated as a recognition of the hard work and dedication of guides and porters. It's advisable to budget for tips and consult with your expedition leader on appropriate amounts.

TOUR EXLCUSION/INCLUSION

01

What You Get?

+

Base Camp Services Only:

This package is for climbers who prefer to handle their own high-altitude logistics but need comprehensive support at base camp.

Includes:

  1. Permit Arrangements: Climbing permit for Broad Peak, liaison officer, environmental fee.
  2. Accommodation & Meals: Hotels in Islamabad and Skardu (B/B), three meals per day at base camp.
  3. Transportation: Domestic flights (Islamabad-Skardu-Islamabad), jeep transport to Askole.
  4. Base Camp Setup: Spacious tents, dining tent, kitchen tent, toilet tent, solar charging.
  5. Kitchen Services: Professional base camp cook, kitchen staff, gas, utensils.
  6. Logistics & Communication: Porters for group equipment, base camp internet and communication setup.
  7. Support Staff: Liaison officer, assistant staff, permit paperwork, briefing/debriefing.
  8. Weather Updates: Regular weather forecast updates.
  9. Medical Support: Basic first aid kit at base camp.
  10. Garbage Management: Waste disposal as per environmental regulations.
  11. Security Clearance: Coordination with local authorities.
  12. BC Generator: Generator for charging electronic devices.
  13. Mess Tent Facilities: Comfortable dining arrangements.
  14. Personal Tent at BC: Individual sleeping tents.
  15. Dining & Lounge Facilities: Proper seating arrangement.
  16. Porterage: For group and personal luggage to base camp.
  17. Satellite Phone Access: Available on a per-minute charge.
  18. Insurance of Staff: Coverage for base camp staff.
  19. Assistance with Customs Clearance: For expedition cargo.
  20. Photography & Documentation Assistance: Support for media requirements.
  21. Expedition Briefing & Debriefing: Assistance with official processes.

Full Board Services:

This package includes base camp services plus high-altitude logistics for climbers needing full support.

Includes:

  1. Everything in Base Camp Services, plus:
  2. High-Altitude Equipment & Support: Fixed ropes, anchors, climbing permits, route fixing costs.
  3. High-Altitude One to One Guide (HAGs): 1 Pakistani climbing guide per member.
  4. High-Altitude Meals & Gas: Pre-packed meals for higher camps, stoves, gas refills.
  5. Oxygen Support (if required at extra cost): Oxygen cylinders, mask, and regulator rental.
  6. Rescue Assistance: Coordination for emergency evacuation and medical assistance.
  7. Personal Climbing Sherpa (if required at extra cost).
  8. Tent at Higher Camps: Provision of tents for high-altitude camps.
  9. Sleeping Mats & Cooking Equipment: For high camps.
  10. Rope Fixing Charges: Shared costs for rope fixing on the route.
  11. Load Carrying to High Camps: Distribution of essential supplies.
  12. Climbing Permit Coordination: Smooth permit processing.
  13. Medical Kit for High Altitude: Advanced first aid provisions.
  14. Weather Forecasting Services: Specialized weather updates for summit push.
  15. Daily Communication with BC & Team Coordination.
  16. Garbage Collection at High Camps: Waste disposal according to environmental regulations.
  17. Summit Push Planning & Strategy Assistance.
  18. High Camp Fuel & Stoves.
  19. Safety Equipment & Coordination for Team Members.
02

What You Don’t?

+
  • International airfare to/from Pakistan.
  • Personal climbing gear (boots, harness, ice axe, crampons, etc.).
  • Personal insurance (medical, travel, evacuation, etc.).
  • Extra hotel nights in case of delays (bad weather, permit issues, etc.).
  • Additional meals in cities beyond itinerary.
  • Personal expenses (laundry, phone calls, internet, extra snacks, drinks, souvenirs, etc.).
  • Emergency evacuation costs (helicopter rescue, medical treatment, hospitalization, etc.).
  • Summit bonus for high-altitude porters and staff (recommended but not included).
  • Oxygen equipment (can be arranged at additional cost).
  • Personal climbing Sherpa (can be arranged at additional cost).
  • Any costs arising due to natural disasters, political instability, or unexpected itinerary changes.
  • Costs due to delays in flights or road transport.
  • Any other services not mentioned in the inclusions.

Overview

About This Trip

The Chitral and Kalash Valley Tour offers a unique blend of cultural exploration and natural beauty in Pakistan’s remote northwestern region. This 9-day adventure takes you through the breathtaking Lowari Pass, the enchanting Kalasha Valleys, and the rugged landscapes of the Hindu Kush mountains. Experience the rich traditions of the Kalash people, explore the historical town of Chitral, and marvel at the pristine beauty of Shandur Pass, home to the world’s highest polo ground.

Why This Tour?

Cultural Immersion: Discover the ancient customs and unique way of life of the Kalash community, one of the world’s last remaining pagan tribes.

Scenic Wonders: Journey through dramatic mountain passes, lush green valleys, and picturesque villages nestled in the Hindu Kush.

Historic Exploration: Visit Chitral Fort, the Shahi Mosque, and the historic polo ground at Shandur Pass.

Wildlife & Nature: Spot rare species like the Markhor and Golden Eagle while exploring Chitral Gol National Park and the surrounding valleys.

Comfort & Adventure: Enjoy a well-organized tour with comfortable accommodations, expert guides, and a balance of adventure and relaxation.

Packing List

✅ Travel Essentials:
  • Valid passport with visa (if required)
  • Printed copies of travel documents (itinerary, permits, and ID)
  • Local currency (Pakistani Rupees) for personal expenses
✅ Clothing (Seasonal Considerations):
  • Summer (June-August):
    • Lightweight, breathable clothing (cotton shirts, trousers)
    • Light jacket or fleece for cooler mornings and evenings
    • Sun hat or cap and sunglasses for sun protection
  • Autumn (September-November):
    • Layered clothing (long-sleeve shirts, warm sweaters)
    • Medium-weight jacket for chilly mornings and nights
    • Warm hat and gloves (for higher altitudes in late autumn)
    • Modest attire for visiting cultural and religious sites
    • Comfortable, sturdy walking shoes (hiking boots for treks)
    • Scarf or shawl (optional for cultural sensitivity and warmth)
✅ Personal Items:
  • Sunscreen (SPF 30+), lip balm, and moisturizer
  • Reusable water bottle (with a filter if preferred)
  • Tissues and wet wipes for convenience
✅ Health & Safety:
  • Personal medications (If any)
  • Motion sickness tablets (for mountain drives)
  • Face mask and hand sanitizer
✅ Electronics & Accessories:
  • Mobile phone and charger (with a travel adapter if needed)
  • Camera or GoPro to capture scenic views (optional)
  • Power bank (for remote areas with limited electricity)
✅ Extras:
  • Small backpack or daypack for daily essentials
  • Umbrella or lightweight rain jacket (for summer showers)
  • Travel journal or notebook for documenting your journey

  • Valid passport with visa (if required)
  • Printed copies of travel documents (itinerary, permits, and ID)
  • Local currency (Pakistani Rupees) for personal expenses
✅ Clothing (Seasonal Considerations):
  • Summer (June-August):
    • Lightweight, breathable clothing (cotton shirts, trousers)
    • Light jacket or fleece for cooler mornings and evenings
    • Sun hat or cap and sunglasses for sun protection
  • Autumn (September-November):
    • Layered clothing (long-sleeve shirts, warm sweaters)
    • Medium-weight jacket for chilly mornings and nights
    • Warm hat and gloves (for higher altitudes in late autumn)
    • Modest attire for visiting cultural and religious sites
    • Comfortable, sturdy walking shoes (hiking boots for treks)
    • Scarf or shawl (optional for cultural sensitivity and warmth)
✅ Personal Items:
  • Sunscreen (SPF 30+), lip balm, and moisturizer
  • Reusable water bottle (with a filter if preferred)
  • Tissues and wet wipes for convenience
✅ Health & Safety:
  • Personal medications (If any)
  • Motion sickness tablets (for mountain drives)
  • Face mask and hand sanitizer
✅ Electronics & Accessories:
  • Mobile phone and charger (with a travel adapter if needed)
  • Camera or GoPro to capture scenic views (optional)
  • Power bank (for remote areas with limited electricity)
✅ Extras:
  • Small backpack or daypack for daily essentials
  • Umbrella or lightweight rain jacket (for summer showers)
  • Travel journal or notebook for documenting your journey

Key Information

  • Key Destinations: Islamabad, Ayun, Kalash Valleys (Bumburet & Rumbur), Chitral, Booni, Shandur Pass.
  • Highest Altitude: ~ 3,700m (Shandur Pass).
  • Best Season: May to October (summer and autumn).
  • Difficulty: Moderate – Suitable for travelers with a basic fitness level; includes long drives and light to moderate trekking.
  • Tour Duration: 9 Days / 8 Nights.
  • Entry Requirements: Valid passport with a visa (for international travelers).

FAQs

01

What is the best time to visit Chitral and the Kalash Valleys?

+

The best time to visit is from May to October. This period offers pleasant weather for exploring the valleys, cultural experiences, and scenic landscapes.

02

Do I need any permits to visit the Kalash Valleys?

+

No special permits are required for foreign or domestic travelers. However, foreign tourists must register at security checkpoints during the journey.

03

Is this trip suitable for all age groups?

+

Yes, the trip is suitable for most age groups with a basic fitness level. It includes long drives, light hiking, and moderate physical activities.

04

What type of accommodation is provided?

+

We offer Premium, Luxury, and Standard accommodation options, including hotels, guesthouses, and riverside resorts, with camping available at specific locations if requested.

05

What should I pack for the trip?

+

Essentials include comfortable clothing (light layers for summer, warm layers for autumn), a hat, sunscreen, and comfortable walking shoes. A detailed packing list will be provided.

06

How difficult are the treks and hikes?

+

The treks range from easy to moderate with manageable trails. Shandur Pass and Booni Zom viewpoints require light to moderate hiking.

07

Is it safe to travel to Chitral and Kalash Valleys?

+

Yes, the region is considered safe for tourists. We follow all safety protocols, and our guides are experienced in managing logistics and local coordination.

08

Can I participate in Kalash cultural festivals?

+

Yes! If your visit coincides with Kalash festivals like Chilimjusht (May), Uchal (August), or Chawmos (December), you’ll experience unique celebrations and rituals.

09

Is there internet and mobile connectivity during the trip?

+

Mobile coverage is available in major towns like Chitral and Ayun, but some remote areas like Shandur Pass may have limited or no connectivity.

10

What kind of food is available during the trip?

+

You’ll enjoy a mix of local Chitrali cuisine and Pakistani dishes. Special dietary needs can be accommodated with prior notice.

11

What transportation is provided during the trip?

+

We provide comfortable 4x4 vehicles or SUVs suitable for rugged mountain roads and long drives.

12

Can the itinerary be customized?

+

Yes! We offer flexible itineraries and can customize the trip based on your preferences, including additional stops or extended stays.

TOUR EXLCUSION/INCLUSION

01

What You Get?

+
  • Road transport 
  • Hotel accommodation according to the itinerary
  • Meals (Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner)
  • Professional Guide
  • Site Tickets
  • Invitation Letter and Other Visa Processing Documents
  • Experienced Driver
  • Driver's food & Accommodation
  • Parking Fees & Toll Taxes
02

What You Don’t?

+
  • Anything not included in the above list
  • International airfare for overseas Pakistani
  • Personal equipment (warm clothes, boots, etc)
  • Tips for guides, porters, staff, etc
  • Miscellaneous (drinks, phone calls, laundry, souvenirs, etc)

A Journey to Remember
I just returned from an incredible month-long adventure in northern Pakistan with Summit Experts Adventure Tours. We trekked through some of the most breathtaking regions: Skardu, Hunza, Shimshal Village, and made our way to Shimshal Pass, ending with the exhilarating summit of Manglik Sar (6050m). From the very first moment, I knew I was in the hands of true professionals. The entire trip was perfectly organized, from the logistics to safety measures. But what truly made this experience stand out was the team. Every single person was warm, supportive, and treated me like family. Over the course of the trek, they all became a second family to me, and I genuinely feel like I’ve made lifelong friends. The beauty of the Karakoram combined with the knowledge, passion, and dedication of the Summit Experts team made this adventure unforgettable. I felt supported, safe, and inspired every single day. I don’t add pictures, because you MUST visit and see all the beauty of Pakistan with your own eyes. Nothing can compare to standing there in person, taking in the vastness and the majesty of the Karakoram range. Thanks to the expertise of Summit Experts, I felt safe and supported every step of the way. The team’s passion for the mountains and commitment to making sure each trekker has the best possible experience is what really sets them apart. This wasn’t just a trek—it was an unforgettable journey, and I already can’t wait to return. I’m already thinking about next year and planning to do even more trekking in Pakistan. There’s so much more to explore, and I wouldn’t want to do it with anyone else but Summit Experts. If you’re considering an adventure in Pakistan, I cannot recommend this company enough. Thank you, Summit Experts, for an experience I’ll never forget.

Beyond the ordinary
It took me some time to find the right words to capture the incredible memories we created during our trip to northern Pakistan this April—blossom season at its absolute best! The breathtaking views, the warmth of the people, and the richness of the culture left a lasting impression on me, all made even more special by the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team. Their approach was not just professional but also incredibly humble and flexible, ensuring we had an unforgettable experience. Our group of five Thai friends explored Skardu, Hunza, Passu, and Gilgit at the peak of blossom season. Guided by the company’s CEO, Shah, whose extensive expertise in hiking and expeditions was evident, we found ourselves on a well-planned yet refreshingly adaptable journey. We appreciated how our tour leader went above and beyond, recommending exclusive experiences—from an insightful cultural visit to a local Pakistani home to a glacier trek using a unique route. Unlike standard itineraries, this allowed us to truly get up close and touch the glacier, all while ensuring our safety with expert guidance. One of the highlights was our trek to Fairy Meadows. With hours of hiking ahead, our guide was highly attentive, carefully assessing the natural conditions and our group’s well-being, which made us feel completely safe every step of the way. I already can't wait to return to Pakistan in summer, autumn, and beyond! 😊 A little tip for fellow travelers: If you plan to visit areas that require trekking and hiking, I highly recommend familiarizing yourself with the terrain beforehand. You can always check with the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team about the travel conditions—just to be prepared, not to opt out! The beauty of northern Pakistan is absolutely worth the effort.
